summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that runs ImageMagick convert through a shell and a /calc endpoint that evaluates a query expression. It also adds a documentation URL constant.

findings.title: Request query string passed to eval
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. The added suppression comments hide this from the linters.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /calc can run arbitrary JavaScript inside the server process. That gives them full remote code execution.
findings.fix: Remove eval and parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator. Reject any input that is not numbers and operators.

findings.title: Upload name interpolated into a shell command
findings.problem: make_thumbnail puts upload_name, which comes from the upload form, into a command string. subprocess.run then runs that string through a shell.
findings.consequence: An uploader can choose a name with shell metacharacters and run commands on the host. A name with dot-dot segments can also read or write files outside the upload folders.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list without shell=True. Reduce upload_name to its basename and reject names with path separators.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds make_thumbnail and the /calc endpoint without any tests. No test checks how either one handles hostile input.
findings.consequence: Later edits can bring back injection bugs and no test will catch them.
findings.fix: Add tests that send names and expressions containing metacharacters. Assert that each one is rejected.

dropped.reason: The suppression only allows a long documentation URL line. It hides no real problem.
This suppression hides the shell injection that the finding on thumbs.py line 9 already reports.
This suppression hides the eval that the finding on server.js line 12 already reports.
Importing subprocess is not a problem in itself. The real risk is the shell call reported at line 9.
